claims.claim: Lifecycle steps 3-5 correctly distinguish barrier publication, false enable-input-d first-write semantics, valid single-thread MMA issue and descriptors, and tcgen05 commit/mbarrier completion from fence-only ordering.

evidence.locator: MMA grammar, issue granularity, D predicate and lifetimes
evidence.observation: The descriptor/predicate/single-thread and D=A*B conditions match.
Commit attaches completion to an mbarrier, while fences order execution without completing the asynchronous MMA.

challenge.check: Use false enable-input-d semantics and the distinct commit/fence specifications.

claims.claim: Lifecycle steps 6-7 correctly require collective legal tcgen05.ld plus wait::ld before register use, reader completion before overwrite/free, matching collective deallocation, and coverage of every kernel exit path.

evidence.locator: ld collectivity, asynchronous completion, wait and lifetimes

evidence.observation: All allocated TMEM must be deallocated collectively with matching address/count/group before exit.

challenge.check: Combine load lifetime with deallocation issue granularity and explicit-exit rule.
challenge.outcome: All readers must finish and all lanes of the designated warp must execute deallocation; exit is not implicit cleanup.
